guideTitle: Best Drill and Impact Driver Combo Kits (2026)
metaTitle: Best Drill and Driver Combo Kits in 2026
metaDescription: Six cordless drill and impact driver combo kits compared on torque, motors, batteries and platform depth, with picks for DIY, remodeling and trades.
expertTake: The DeWalt DCK277D2 is the combo kit most buyers should choose, because it pairs two brushless compact tools with two batteries on a very deep platform. The Black+Decker BD2KITCDDI is the budget pick for occasional use. If you already own a good drill, skip the combo and buy only an impact driver, since duplicating a drill adds weight to your tool bag without adding capability.
introParagraphs: A combo kit bundles a drill driver and an impact driver on one battery platform, and the box usually advertises the total value of the pieces rather than how well they work together. Two tools sharing batteries and a charger is a real convenience, but only if each tool in the kit is genuinely good.
This guide explains how torque, motor type and battery capacity change daily use, why platform choice matters more than the first kit, and where cheap bundles cut corners.

products.name: DeWalt DCK277D2 20V MAX Brushless Drill and Impact Driver Combo
products.description:
The DCK277D2 puts a compact brushless drill and a compact brushless impact driver in one kit, each about 7.6 inches long. That size lets you work between studs and inside cabinets, while the brushless motors improve run time. A bright LED stays lit for 20 seconds after you release the trigger.

It is a refined step up from the older DeWalt DCK240C2 combo, which uses brushed tools. It is lighter than the Greenworks pair and more compact than the Milwaukee in the group. The motors are not built for heavy framing all day, but they cover nearly everything a homeowner or remodeler does.

Two batteries and a bag mean you can drill while the other pack charges. Buy it if you want a platform you can grow with, because bare tools for 20V MAX are everywhere. Keep bits in the bag and the batteries off hot dashboards. Spare bits and a second bag are cheap add-ons that make the kit feel complete.
products.bestFor: Homeowners and remodelers building a long term tool collection.
pros: Two brushless compact tools in one kit
7.6 inch length fits tight framing bays
Two batteries and a bag included
Platform has the broadest bare tool range
cons: Compact tools lack framing level torque

products.name: Milwaukee 2892-22CT M18 Compact Brushless Drill and Impact Driver Combo

specList.label: Tools
specList.value: Compact drill driver and impact driver

products.description:
The Milwaukee 2892-22CT pairs a compact M18 brushless drill driver and a compact impact driver with two batteries. The brushless motors give longer run time and cooler operation, and the compact bodies suit overhead work and tight spaces. Milwaukee's M18 line is known for durability and a huge professional tool range.

Compared with the DeWalt DCK277D2 it sits in a similar compact class and a similar price class, so the choice often comes down to platform loyalty. Compared with the Craftsman and Black+Decker kits it feels like a professional step up, built for daily use. The Greenworks pair is lighter, but the Milwaukee tools have the stronger service reputation.

Ownership benefits include wide availability of replacement parts and a deep stock of M18 bare tools. If you are likely to buy a sawzall, grinder or fan later, M18 offers every one. Keep the batteries on a platform charger rather than a generic one to protect the cells.
products.bestFor: Tradespeople and serious users who value durability and platform depth.
pros: Brushless compact tools suit all day use
Two batteries and charger included
M18 platform covers hundreds of tools
Compact bodies work overhead
cons: Platform lock-in raises long term cost

products.name: Craftsman V20 RP Brushless Drill and Impact Driver Combo
products.description:
The Craftsman V20 RP kit uses brushless motors in both tools and quotes a drill speed of 1,900 rpm. Its impact driver is designed to be 27 percent shorter than a previous model, which helps in tight spaces. Two batteries and a charger make it a complete package.

It competes directly with the DeWalt DCK277D2, usually at a lower price, and offers similar compact brushless features. The platform is smaller than DeWalt's or Milwaukee's, which limits the bare tool selection later. For many homeowners that tradeoff is acceptable, because they need a few good tools, not hundreds.

It suits weekend work, small decks and home projects. Store the batteries indoors, and update to higher capacity packs if run time falls short. Registering the kit for the warranty is quick and worth doing at purchase.
products.bestFor: Value minded homeowners who want brushless tools.
pros: Brushless drill and impact driver
Impact driver is a short compact design
Two batteries and a charger included
Lower cost than DeWalt and Milwaukee
cons: Smaller platform than the big brands
Less proven for daily trade use

products.name: Greenworks 24V Brushless Drill and Impact Driver Combo
products.description:
The Greenworks 24V combo gives a 400 in-lbs drill and an impact driver rated at 1,950 in-lbs, which is higher than the DeWalt DCF845 class. Both tools are brushless, and the whole kit weighs 4.7 lb, so it is easy on your arms during repetitive work. The 1/2 inch drill chuck is the same size as the DeWalt tools.

The tradeoff is platform. Greenworks 24V is popular for outdoor and garden tools, so a combo kit can share batteries with a mower or trimmer. It does not have the pro trade support of DeWalt or Milwaukee, and the torque numbers should be read as maker claims.

It is a good fit for a household that wants one battery for yard and shop. Keep the chargers dry and the batteries cool. Check the shared battery against the yard tools you already own before ordering.
products.bestFor: Households that want shared batteries with Greenworks yard tools.
pros: Impact driver rated at 1,950 in-lbs
Whole kit weighs only 4.7 lb
Brushless motors in both tools
Batteries share a yard tool platform
cons: Smaller service network than big brands

products.name: Dekopro 20V Brushless Drill and Impact Driver Set
products.description:
The Dekopro set advertises 443 in-lbs on the drill and up to 1,770 in-lbs on the impact driver, both brushless, with two 2.0 Ah batteries and a charger that fills in about an hour. Those figures sit close to the compact DeWalt class on paper, at a much lower purchase price. For a casual user who needs two tools quickly, that is an appealing deal.

The weakness is the ecosystem. Compared with the Craftsman V20 RP or the DeWalt DCK277D2, the Dekopro batteries fit nothing else, and support depends on the seller. Torque numbers are maker claims and may differ from independent figures.

Treat it as a complete starter kit rather than a platform. Expect to replace the whole set if a battery fails years from now.
products.bestFor: Budget buyers who want brushless tools in one box.
pros: Both tools use brushless motors
Two 2.0 Ah batteries and fast charger
443 in-lbs drill torque claim is strong
Lowest cost of the brushless kits

buyingCriteria.explanation: The first kit is cheap compared with the batteries and tools you add later. DeWalt 20V MAX and Milwaukee M18 offer hundreds of bare tools, while the Dekopro offers none. A bundle that locks you into a dead end costs more over ten years. Choose the platform first and then the kit. The common mistake is pricing only the box today. A kit with a dead end platform means buying a whole new set the first time you want a saw, so count that cost in.

Brushless motors run cooler and last longer per charge. The DeWalt DCK277D2, Milwaukee 2892-22CT, Craftsman V20 RP, Greenworks and Dekopro kits use them, while the Black+Decker BD2KITCDDI is brushed. For daily work the extra cost is worth it. For one weekend a year it is not. For a homeowner who drives screws on weekends, brushless is a nice upgrade rather than a need. The gain shows up as fewer charger swaps during a deck build.

A drill at 400 in-lbs and an impact driver near 1,800 in-lbs cover most home work. The Greenworks combo quotes 400 and 1,950, the Dekopro 443 and 1,770. Use those as a rough benchmark. Be wary of any kit that quotes extreme torque without a brand name behind it. As a rule of thumb, any drill under 300 in-lbs will struggle with large auger bits. Check that both tools in the kit, not just the headline one, meet that bar.

Two 2.0 Ah batteries give about double the work of one. Most good kits include two, as in the DeWalt, Milwaukee, Craftsman and Dekopro sets. A single battery means waiting for a charger. Count the packs in the box. Look closely at the kit contents list, because some bundles count a bag or a tape measure as value. The batteries and the tools themselves are what you pay for.

Compact tools reach between studs and inside cabinets. The DeWalt DCK277D2 measures 7.6 inches, and the Craftsman V20 RP impact driver is a shorter design. Heavier full size tools trade access for torque. Think about the spaces you work in. Remember that tool length matters most for overhead work and between joists. Longer tools gain leverage but lose reach into confined spots.

A 3/8 inch chuck limits large bits, as on the Black+Decker drill. A 1/2 inch chuck on the DeWalt, Craftsman and Greenworks drills holds more. A numbered clutch protects screws. Check both before buying. Test the chuck by hand when you can, since a loose chuck on a new tool is a warning sign. Clutch rings should click distinctly and not slip.

specDecoder.meaning: A motor with electronic commutation instead of carbon brushes. It runs cooler, lasts longer and gives more run time. Most modern pro tools use it.
specDecoder.watchFor: Cheap kits label brushless but pair it with a weak battery or gearbox.

specDecoder.meaning: Twisting force measured in inch pounds. Drills of 400 to 500 in-lbs and impact drivers of 1,500 to 1,800 in-lbs are typical. Numbers differ by test method.
specDecoder.watchFor: Unknown brands quote peak torque that is not sustained.

specDecoder.meaning: Battery capacity. A 2.0 Ah pack gives about twice the run time of a 1.0 Ah pack. Weight rises with capacity.
specDecoder.watchFor: Kits include small packs to hit a price point.

specDecoder.meaning: 20V MAX, M18 and 24V describe the battery family. Voltage names are partly marketing. What matters is how many tools share the pack.
specDecoder.watchFor: 20V MAX is not stronger than 18V, since both are the same pack voltage under load.

specDecoder.meaning: Numbered torque settings on the drill. A higher count gives finer control. Drill mode bypasses the clutch.
specDecoder.watchFor: The number of positions matters less than the smoothness of the trigger.

howWeEvaluated.title: Tool pair quality
howWeEvaluated.description: We judged each kit on both the drill and the impact driver, noting torque claims such as 443 and 1,770 in-lbs on the Dekopro. Brushless pairs ranked above brushed. A weak tool in the pair lowered the kit.

howWeEvaluated.title: Battery contents
howWeEvaluated.description: We counted batteries and checked their capacity. Two packs earned credit and fast chargers were noted. Single pack kits lost points.

howWeEvaluated.title: Platform depth
howWeEvaluated.description: DeWalt 20V MAX and Milwaukee M18 lead for tool range, with Craftsman V20 and Greenworks 24V behind. Proprietary packs on the Dekopro rated lowest. Long term cost drove the ranking.

howWeEvaluated.title: Size and weight
howWeEvaluated.description: The DeWalt DCK277D2 is 7.6 inches long and the Greenworks kit weighs 4.7 lb. We credited compact bodies and low weight. Ergonomics matter on repetitive jobs.

howWeEvaluated.title: Lineup positioning
howWeEvaluated.description: The DCK277D2 leads on balance, the Milwaukee on durability and the Craftsman on value. Greenworks is the light yard friendly kit and Dekopro the budget brushless. The Black+Decker is the entry level choice.

cards.label: Big platform
cards.text: DeWalt 20V MAX and Milwaukee M18 have hundreds of bare tools. You pay more up front for lower cost later. Both the DCK277D2 and 2892-22CT fit here.

cards.label: Value platform
cards.text: Craftsman V20, Greenworks 24V and Dekopro cost less now but offer fewer tools. They suit buyers who need a few tools.

howToChoose.note: If you will own many tools, pick DeWalt or Milwaukee. If you will own three, pick on price.

cards.label: Look for
cards.text: Compact bodies, LED lights and two batteries. Work in tight spaces rewards short tools. Brushless motors cut heat in long sessions.

cards.label: In this comparison
cards.text: The DeWalt DCK277D2 and Milwaukee 2892-22CT are best, with compact brushless tools. The Craftsman V20 RP is a good value option.

cards.label: Spend more if
cards.text: You use tools weekly or will add more. The DeWalt DCK277D2 or Milwaukee 2892-22CT pays back.

cards.label: Save if
cards.text: You need basic tools a few times a year. The Black+Decker or Dekopro kit is enough.

maintenance.why: Lithium cells age faster when full or empty. Keep them indoors.
Dust blocks cooling air. Blow it out with compressed air.
A loose chuck lets bits slip. A dirty collet prevents bit lock.
Worn bits waste torque. They also damage screw heads.
Loose bits and batteries get damaged. A tidy bag speeds setup.

faq.q: Is a combo kit better than buying tools separately?
faq.a: Usually yes for beginners, since two tools plus batteries cost less in a kit. Buy separately if you already own batteries.

faq.q: Do I need both a drill and an impact driver?
faq.a: Most people end up wanting both. The drill handles holes and delicate screws, while the impact driver drives large fasteners.
DeWalt 20V MAX and Milwaukee M18 have the broadest ranges. Pick the one that sells the other tools you want.

faq.q: Is brushless worth the extra cost?
faq.a: For regular use, yes. It gives more run time and less heat.

faq.q: How many batteries do I need?
faq.a: Two is enough for most jobs, since one charges while you use the other. Heavy users may want a third.
No. They are the same battery voltage under load, with 20V MAX being a peak rating.
